{{nihongo|'''Mount Haguro'''|羽黒山|''Haguro-san''}} is one of the [[Three Mountains of Dewa]] in the city of [[Tsuruoka, Yamagata|Tsuruoka]], the ancient province of [[Dewa Province|Dewa]] (a domain consisting of modern-day [[Yamagata Prefecture]] and [[Akita Prefecture]]), [[Japan]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Hagurosan｜Dewa Sanzan Shrine formula homepage |url=http://www.dewasanzan.jp/en/publics/index/47/ |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=Dewa Sanzan Shrine official site |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Haguro-san |url=https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e7902.html |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=www.japan-guide.com |language=en}}</ref> [[Dewa Shrine]] is located on Mount Haguro.

==Access==
The summit can also be reached by bus service. In addition to religious pilgrims, travellers often stay at the [[Saikan]] temple lodging. In the [[Edo period]], there used to be 336 [[shukubo]] on the mountain.<ref>Earhart, H. B. (1965). Four Ritual Periods of Haguro Shugendō in Northeastern Japan. ''History of Religions'', ''5''(1), 93–113. {{JSTOR|1061805}}</ref>

Visitors can visit the official english website of the Dewa Sanzan Mountains for updates on the opening and closing of the mountains as well as other access information. <ref>https://thedewasanzan.com/</ref>
